chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Miskeen al-Samman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who bought a female slave who had been stolen from the land of truce (Saghib). He said: 'He should return her to the one from whom he bought her, and he should not approach her if he is able to find him or if he is wealthy.' I said: 'May I be your ransom, for he has died and his descendants have died.' He said: 'Then he should pay her price (compensation).'

key_terms.أَرْضِ الصُّلْحِ: Land of truce; territory under a peace treaty with Muslims

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a buyer of a stolen slave from the land of truce if the original owner is deceased?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the status of a female slave acquired from a region under a peace treaty (*Ard al-Sulh*) who was subsequently stolen, emphasizing the protection of the buyer's rights. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between two scenarios: if the original owner is alive and capable, the slave is returned without the buyer consummating the union to avoid uncertainty in ownership; if the owner and his descendants have passed away, the buyer retains her by paying her value (*istis'a*), ensuring equitable compensation. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle of balancing property rights with the practicalities of ownership transfer in cases of theft from treaty-protected lands.
